text:
mira: quick heads-up — ran the AWQ hybrid sweep (group-size / act-quant grid) against the new 13B bring-up. seeing a weird class of intermittent token-level degradations during serving that don't show up in batch evals.

sam: can you paste the minimal repro logs? is it deterministic on a single seed?

mira: short log snippet from a failing serve trace:```
[2026-03-18 09:12:41] req=abcd1234 model=rw-13b-awq group=64 actq=2 latency=42ms tokens=16 status=200
[2026-03-18 09:12:41] decode_step=7 kv_hit=false prefix_len=12 group_idx=2 sample_entropy=2.9
[2026-03-18 09:12:41] generated="...and the meeting will be at t" expected="...and the meeting will be at 3"
```
Looks like a subtle off-by-one in prefix KV lookup? only on live-ish long-prefix requests. batch eval (short ctx) is fine.

devon: interesting — did the same workload with GPTQ and FP8 variants?

mira: yup. GPTQ/FP8 variants are stable. AWQ hybrid (group=64, actq=2) passes offline eval: ppl and rouge within 0.3% but ~0.6% token-level mismatch on long prefix samples under serving.

frida: any correlation with cold-start / cache warmup? could be KV cache misrouting under group splits.

mira: strong correlation with warmup windows. if we send a quick coherence probe first, later requests are fine. if the probe omitted, mismatch appears in ~1/1500 requests.

kate: maybe the group sharding causes race when KV pages are promoted. Can you capture a binary diff of kv-index on failure?

mira: captured a small repro payload and mem dump. here's a minimal shell command to reproduce locally (staging):
```bash
export RW_MODEL=rw-13b-awq-hybrid
python run_stress.py --seq 1024 --prefix 768 --group-size 64 --act-quant 2 --seed 42 --rps 10
```
Repro rate ~0.06% per request, but deterministic with the same seed.

devon: thanks. I'll run with instrumentation on KV prefetch and add additional asserts around prefix len and group boundary.

sam: also please try forcing group-size=32 and group-size=128 to see if anomaly scales with group count.

mira: done quick: group=32 -> no failures in 10k requests; group=128 -> failures jump 3x. so seems non-linear with group count.

frida: that sounds like an indexing math bug when group crosses cache page boundary. does act-quant level change anything? (actq=1 vs 2)

mira: actq=1 reduced but didn't eliminate. actq=3 made it slightly worse. so both group boundary and actq interplay.

kate: can we mitigate in prod by routing long-prefix requests to the GPTQ variant for now? minimize risk while we patch.

mira: we already have fallback rule; rolling it on for specific customers now. planning a canary rollback schedule.

ops-bot: deploy plan created: canary rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100%, monitor token-mismatch rate and latency.

devon: for fix we should add unit tests exercising group boundary offsets and a sanitizer in runtime that logs when a prefix lookup index != expected_index. If mismatch rate > threshold, auto-fallback.

sam: also add a small eval that simulates long-user histories (prefix 512+) during bakeoffs. most of our offline suites were too short.

mira: Agreed. I'll open a PR with tests + a patch to boundary calc. will attach the memdump and repro in the PR.

frida: can we add a quick metric in console: "kv-prefix-mismatch-rate" so product teams can see early signs?

kate: yep, I'll add a derived metric from tracer events. thresholds: warn at 0.01% and alert at 0.1% per model.

mira: thanks — will post PR and ping y'all. Also note: this is a good reminder that AWQ bakeoffs need a long-prefix stress step in staging; adding to bake checklist.

sam: nice find. small ask — include a short note in the bakeoff doc referencing these parameters (group size, act-quant, warmup probe) so next onboards don't miss it. :thumbsup:

mira: will do. ending thread with list of actions in the PR.
